identification: Set of three William IV / early Victorian bar-back dining chairs, c1840-1860: deep curved top rail (bar back), plain curved mid rail, slightly sabre back uprights, stuff-over/drop-in seats in brown leather (one, left, paler and more scuffed, possibly a different hide), seat rail with applied moulding, ring-turned tapering front legs on peg toes, plain splayed back legs. Timber reddish-brown with a dull old finish; colour and the plain rails fit Australian colonial cedar as catalogued but could equally be mahogany (no end grain visible). Tasmanian/Australian colonial bar-back form. Estimate 100-150, current bid about A$50-55 (next increment 60).
